subject: Benchmark ops playbook — prompt soak, acceptance gates, and measurement definitions
messages:
From: Paul Reynolds <paul@novaretail.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Novaretail Infra Team <infra@novaretail.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up — high-level perf targets

Thanks again for the call today. Couple quick clarifying items from our side as we line up internal approval for a benchmark run:

- Latency targets: our product team is aiming for p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 450ms for the 256-token typical generation path. For longer generations (~1k tokens) we need p95 <= 700ms.
- Concurrency: baseline 40 concurrent active sessions per region, ability to burst to 180 for short spikes (2–5 mins).
- Streaming: we use chunked responses (150–300 token chunks). Important that first-byte latency for stream start is low (<120ms) and that per-chunk latency is consistent (jitter < 60ms).

We can provide the prompt corpus (mixed prod + synthetic) and infra diagram — attaching the latter. Goal is to run a qualification window next week (Mar 20–21).

Can you outline measurement definitions and what you need from us to make the run reproducible?

—Paul
Novaretail — Senior PM

Attachment: novaretail-infra-diagram.pdf (diagram, 120KB)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Paul Reynolds <paul@novaretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discovery follow-up — high-level perf targets

Thanks Paul — great context and helpful targets. Recap + proposed ops playbook below so we're aligned before the run next week.

Recap of your targets (as I heard them):
- Short gen (256 tokens): p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 450ms
- Long gen (~1k tokens): p95 <= 700ms
- Sustained concurrency: 40 active sessions/region; burst to 180 for 2–5m
- Streaming: first-byte <120ms; per-chunk jitter <60ms

Proposed run plan (high-level):
1) Prompt soak (warmup): run a 30-minute soak with a representative mixture from your prompt corpus to populate KV cache/prefix cache. This stabilizes cold-warm transitions.
2) Steady-state qualification: 60-minute steady window at target sustained concurrency (40) measuring p50/p90/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.
3) Burst test: 3x 5-minute bursts to 180 concurrent sessions spaced by 10 minutes to observe scaling/fallback behavior.
4) Streaming correctness + jitter: run chunked stream sampling across 1000 streams distributed over the steady-state window, measure first-byte and inter-chunk latency distributions.
5) Repro check: re-run a short subset (10-minute) later the same day with identical seed/prompt order to verify reproducibility.

What we need from you before Monday (Mar 19):
- Prompt bundle (jsonl) with production proportions and labels for routing/intent (we need the file format we discussed). Please send by EOD Fri Mar 16.
- A single IP allowlist range or test credentials for an account we can use to hit your staging VPC.
- Confirmation of whether any request-level pre-/post-processing modifies tokenization (we need deterministic tokenization).

Attachments I'll share from our side before the run: prompt soak script, harness config, and a measurement-spec spreadsheet (see attachments).

Acceptance gate (proposal): pass if during steady-state: >= 95% of requests meet p95 target and p99 regressions less than 10% vs baseline; streaming first-byte target met for >= 93% of streams. We can tighten thresholds for final acceptance.

Next steps: Ben will share the harness spec + seed control details; Karthik will confirm metrics definitions and where to pull logs (trace ids, token-level timing). If that all looks good, can we lock Mar 20 for the soak + qualification?

—Chloe Martin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Benchmark ops playbook — prompt soak, acceptance gates, and measurement definitions

Appended some measurement/harness details so Novaretail can prep: feel free to forward to infra.

Measurement definitions (short):
- p50/p90/p95/p99: end-to-end service latency measured client-side from request send to last-token-received for generation calls. Streaming first-byte is measured from request send to first-byte received. Inter-chunk latency is the delta between successive chunk arrivals at the client.
- Warmup vs steady-state: warmup includes the 30m soak where we do not include results in acceptance calculations; steady-state is the 60m window after warmup.
- Determinism: we control seeds at the harness level; for quantized/deterministic runs we will pin model variant + RNG seed. Note: some community models still have nondeterministic kernels — we will call that out in results.

Harness config notes:
- Ramp: 0 -> 40 over 5 minutes for steady-state; bursts are instant ramp spikes we simulate via controlled load generators.
- Token accounting: we will report tokens generated per request and normalize costs using your sample distribution.
- KV/prefix cache measurement: the harness will emit a KV-hit boolean per request; please ensure any proxy or token-munging does not strip the cache key header.
- Log artifacts: we will produce per-request CSV with request id, start_ts, first_byte_ts, last_byte_ts, tokens_generated, kv_hit, model_variant. This will be uploaded to the shared Drive link.

Attachment: novaretail-prompt-bundle.jsonl (please verify ordering matches your prod proportions).

I can run a dry-run on Mar 19 in the afternoon to validate connectivity and tokenization.

—Ben
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Paul Reynolds <paul@novaretail.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 07:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Benchmark ops playbook — prompt soak, acceptance gates, and measurement definitions

Couple of concrete definitions and acceptance thresholds from the eng side to avoid ambiguity during analysis:

Metric definitions:
- p95 for short gen = 95th percentile of client-side end-to-end latency measured over the steady-state window. We use histogram-based aggregation with 1ms buckets.
- p99 regressions: computed relative to the warm baseline (the first steady-state run). A failing regression is when p99 increases by >10% and the increase is statistically significant (Mann-Whitney U, p<0.05).
- Streaming first-byte: include only requests that result in at least one token; aborted or empty responses excluded.

Reproducibility controls:
- Prompt order: harness will accept a seed parameter and use deterministic shuffling; the prompt-bundle must preserve an id field per line for exact replay.
- Model variant pinning: we'll run on a pinned model sha and separately on your quantized variant (if you want quantized numbers).
- Artifact retention: we will provide the raw CSV + aggregated histograms and an artifact tarball for 90 days.

Pass/fail gate (engineering):
- Short-gen p95 <= 200ms for >= 95% of samples during steady-state.
- Short-gen p99 <= 450ms or p99 regression <= 10% (whichever is stricter).
- Burst behavior: no >10% increase in error rate or >25% increase in p95 during bursts vs steady-state.
- Streaming: first-byte <120ms for >= 93% of streams; inter-chunk jitter median <40ms.

I'll upload a formal measurement-spec.xlsx with these definitions and example CSV columns to the Drive folder and add brief instructions on how to format the prompt ids.

—Karthik
Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
